clue.text: Refashioned "A" from Ascot in official device

indicators.note: something refashioned is remade in a new shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: all ten letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A racecourse letter is redesigned as part of an official emblem at Royal Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks tempt you to treat "A" as a single letter to move about; in fact the whole phrase A FROM ASCOT is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic emblem granted to a family, town or institution is a formal insignia, an official device.

clue.text: Mould in shed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shape metal by pouring it into a form
second meaning: to throw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mildew growing in a garden shed, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both forming molten metal in a mould and discarding something, as a snake sloughs its skin.

clue.text: Animated roadmen notice returning Galaxy

indicators.note: animated means lively and set in motion, so the letters of the following word are stirred up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the short word for notice is read backwards

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Lively road workers spot a returning Ford Galaxy car on their stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large spiral galaxy to our Milky Way, so the name stands for a galaxy.

clue.text: Cat at any time eating mouse's heart

indicators.note: something eating another thing takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: once can mean at any time, as in 'if once you start'

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only the middle of the five-letter word is kept

parts.note: the central letter of mouse

explanation.surface: A cat is always ready to eat the heart of a mouse it has caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big wild cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Want bishop to interrupt bizarre seance

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so the one letter goes inside the other piece
bizarre means weird and out of order, so the following word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman wants to break up a strange spiritualist meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Want is a noun here, meaning lack, not a verb meaning desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or shortage means the same as the noun for something not being present.

clue.text: Old puffer in shopping centre on a road

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
taken as written
the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An elderly smoker stands in a shopping centre beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A puffer is a steam locomotive (puffing billy); Mallard is the famous British engine that set the steam speed record in 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: The record-breaking 1938 steam locomotive Mallard is a historic engine, so an old puffing train.

clue.text: Unlikely way to downsize corporation?

parts.note: surface reading: an odd strategy for cutting the size of a big company
setter's reading: corporation is old British slang for a pot belly, which you reduce by dieting

explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is jocular British slang for a large paunch; to downsize that you go on a diet, so the verb is the 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose weight by dieting reduces a paunch, which is an unlikely method for shrinking a business.

clue.text: Girl in line with distinctive character

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
an aura is a distinctive atmosphere or character

explanation.surface: A girl standing in a queue has a distinctive air about her.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a common girl's given name, the usual crossword pattern of a name defined by Girl.

clue.text: In dressing many a one is transformed

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: all ten letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: Putting on smart clothes, plenty of people find themselves changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a sauce for salad, and this creamy egg-and-oil emulsion is a classic one.

clue.text: Stick at defending peace proposal

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so the outer word wraps round what follows

parts.note: taken as written
sh is a call for peace and quiet
a plan is a proposal

explanation.surface: Someone holds firm while protecting a peace proposal in talks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick cut from an ash sapling, so a stick in the literal sense.

clue.text: Irishman protecting daughter covered chair

indicators.note: protecting means shielding on all sides, so the name wraps round the single letter

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An Irish father shelters his daughter under a covered seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, so the short form names that covered chair.

clue.text: Old PM clear: army trains here

parts.note: Lord Salisbury was Prime Minister three times under Queen Victoria
plain means clear, obvious

explanation.surface: A former prime minister makes it obvious that the army goes there to train.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury Plain is a chalk plateau in Wiltshire, England, used as the British Army's largest training area.
explanation.definitionFit: This Wiltshire upland is the British Army's main training ground, so the place where soldiers drill.

clue.text: Sea current advanced in Orwellian superstate

parts.note: an ocean is a large sea
I is the physics symbol for electric current
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A sea current pushes forward within the world of an Orwell novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four the world is split into three blocs, and Oceania is the one Winston lives in.

clue.text: See 11
Hopeless idea main or pudding suggests?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plan with no chance of success
second meaning, playful: a main course or dessert is not the first course of a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer literally: a main or a pudding is a course that is not the opening course.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme with no prospect of getting going is called this, and literally it means a dish that is not the first course.

clue.text: Be responsible for stanza in Old English

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, so the poem section sits within the language abbreviation

parts.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
a verse is a stanza of a poem

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of a stanza written in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise something is to have charge of it, which is the sense of being responsible for it.

clue.text: Greek character cheers, collecting first of top marks

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the selected letter is taken inside the earlier pieces

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: first of picks out only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of top

explanation.surface: A Greek person cheers, collecting the best grades in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta and cheers are both casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks resembling Christ's wounds, and more generally the plural of a stigma, a mark of disgrace.

clue.text: Inactive marine mammal losing tail in lake

indicators.note: losing its tail means the animal's name drops its final letter

parts.note: dead means inactive, as in a dead volcano
a seal is a sea-dwelling mammal

explanation.surface: A lazy sea creature with a missing tail lies in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, despite its name.

clue.text: Little inclination to include suitable candidates

parts.note: short means little in height or length
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone has little desire to take in the suitable applicants.
explanation.walkthrough: Inclination here means a physical tilt, as when a ship lists, not a desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A final selection of applicants considered fit for a job is a list of suitable candidates.

clue.text: Endurance damaged mast in Antarctica primarily

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Antarctica

explanation.surface: A polar expedition shows endurance after a ship's mast is damaged in the Antarctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the capacity for prolonged effort, which is endurance.

clue.text: State captivated by brigand or racketeer

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive within, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of brigand, the whole of or and the start of racketeer

explanation.surface: A country falls under the spell of a bandit or gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny independent principality in the Pyrenees, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Such sausage rolls anathema to cool cats?

definitions.text: Such sausage rolls anathema to cool cats?

parts.note: surface reading: a kind of sausage in a bread roll
setter's reading: cool jazz fans dislike anything hot, and cats hate dogs, so these are doubly loathed

explanation.walkthrough: Cool cats is slang for hip jazz fans; they shun anything hot, and literal cats hate dogs, so both halves of the snack's name repel them.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a long bun is a sausage roll of this type, and the name splits into heat and canines.

clue.text: Security men only breaking tool

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the party word goes inside the implement

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool
stag describes a men-only party or event

explanation.surface: Guards, all male, break a tool during a security check.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag night is a British bachelor party, so stag means men only.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held as a pledge that terms will be met is kept as security, the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Fear American with large weapon

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: People fear a US citizen carrying a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or anxiety at a danger, a near synonym for fear.

clue.text: Well-briefed leader of army fighting Spain

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of army
war is fighting
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: An army commander is fully informed about fighting in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well briefed has been given the facts, so is informed about the situation.

clue.text: Remote part in Kurdistan trail

indicators.note: part in says the answer is a portion found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the middle of Kurdistan into the start of trail

explanation.surface: A remote section of a mountain path in Kurdistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remote is far away, which is the plain sense of the answer.

clue.text: More in middle: tons in two areas for vessel

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the two letters that follow

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, taken twice

indicators.note: in middle keeps only the central letters of the word, dropping its ends

parts.note: the central two letters of more
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: More cargo goes in the middle: tons placed in two areas of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is just punctuation; the two A's are the bread of a sandwich with the other pieces as filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel leaving the heart.

clue.text: Secure extra portion did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks how something sounds when spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: more is an extra portion, as in asking for more

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you wanted to secure an extra helping.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to make it fast to a quay or buoy, so to secure it.

clue.text: Display too much skill around restaurant

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the whole string of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to air is to display, as in airing views
OTT is short for over the top
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A show-off parades excessive talent around a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Display too much skill reads like one phrase about showing off, but it splits into three words strung together and then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating place, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Money one might charge incautious tourist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old British slang for cash
second meaning: a large horned animal that may charge at a careless visitor on safari

explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like billing a tourist too much money, which fits the first sense; in fact it is the animal's headlong rush.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is dated British slang for cash, and also the thick-skinned African beast known for charging.

clue.text: Are we told to nurture flightless creature?

indicators.note: are we told hints at something heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: to rear is to nurture and bring up

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether we are meant to care for a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech, where the final R of rear is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American bird that cannot fly, like a small ostrich.

clue.text: Evil-doer's Y-chromosome?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a criminal or wrongdoer
second meaning, read as two words: the element that makes a person male

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining two meanings; split into two words the answer describes what the Y chromosome does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a criminal, and split in two the word names the genetic element determining a man's sex.
